title: Converge GPU dep init: deterministic symbol resolution + staged kernel hotstart
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: node cold-start variance and intermittent symbol resolution failures when heterogeneous kernel bundles (multiple CUTLASS/Triton combinations) are present. Root causes identified in runtime telemetry: non-deterministic .so load ordering, lazy relocation race during concurrent worker start, and probe path that triggers heavy I/O and repeated stat calls on first N requests.

Goal: implement a deterministic kernel initialization pipeline that pre-resolves symbol tables for approved kernel bundles, introduces a lightweight prelink-inspired hotstart stage to satisfy early RPCs, and provide a toggleable runtime mode for staged rollout. This should reduce startup jitter, eliminate a class of symbol lookup failures, and provide safe rollback hooks for Canary.

Scope:
- deterministic shared-object discovery and load order guarantees for GPU kernel bundles
- early pre-resolve pass that runs in a low-priority background thread during agent boot (optionally pinned to a single core)
- canary-able feature-flag to enable/disable hotstart per fleet/region
- runtime telemetry and new metrics: kernel_init_latency_p50/p95, kernel_probe_io_ops, unresolved_symbol_errors
- integration tests and a small e2e canary (dev -> perf -> canary -> global)
acceptance_criteria: 1) Kernel init p95 reduced by >=40% across mixed-bundle testbed compared to baseline (measured on perf cluster). 2) Unresolved symbol error rate drops to <0.01% on first 1k requests during cold start. 3) Feature flagged rollout works: canary machines opt-in, monitoring detects regressions and automatic rollback script succeeds. 4) CI covers simulated mixed CUTLASS/Triton combinations with deterministic ordering enabled.
